title: Safe automatic models for specialists — build this flow?
lead: When no specialist model is selected, YouCoded will use a safe default for the conversation’s provider instead of inheriting an expensive conversation model. These three pictures cover the recovery path when no safe default is available.

steps.path: A specialist hire when no safe automatic model is available
steps.headline: Stop the specialist before it can inherit an expensive model, then offer one direct route to its settings.
steps.changed: The failed hire explains that nothing started and why. Choose specialist models opens Assistant settings directly on Specialists.
steps.notice: The warning stays inside the specialist card, beside the hire that needs attention; it does not create a separate popup.
steps.risk: This deliberately refuses the hire until the user chooses a model if the curated provider defaults are unavailable.

steps.headline: An unset tier says exactly what it means: “No Selection – Model will be chosen automatically.”
steps.changed: The user’s saved value remains empty. At runtime, Automatic follows the active conversation’s provider; an explicit selection still overrides every provider globally.
steps.notice: Users with several providers do not see a misleading single model here—the automatic choice depends on the conversation they are in.
steps.risk: The exact automatic model is intentionally not promised in this row because curated defaults will change as providers release models.

steps.path: Return after saving the missing tier
steps.headline: After the required tier is saved, the same card changes its action to Try again.
steps.changed: The settings button remains until the app confirms that the relevant tier was saved. It then becomes Try again and asks the assistant to repeat the original specialist hire as a visible turn.
steps.notice: The original task, specialist type, tier and work folder are preserved; the retry is not a silent background action.
steps.risk: Trying again adds a short visible retry turn to the conversation rather than secretly replaying an old tool call.
